chunks: And beware of self-admiration, having reliance in what appears good in yourself, and love of exaggerated praise, for this is one of the most reliable opportunities for Satan in himself, to obliterate what is from the good deeds of the virtuous.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual dangers of self-admiration and love of praise in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this foundational instruction for governance, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies self-admiration (al-ijbab) and the love of flattery as critical spiritual vulnerabilities that allow Satan to nullify the good deeds of the righteous. This advice underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on inner purity (tazkiyah) as a prerequisite for just leadership, warning that external praise can mask internal corruption.
